skill.name: google-image-api-skill
skill.description: Extract structured Google Images metadata through the BrowserAct API. The skill prepares search parameters, starts a workflow task, polls status, and returns image result fields when available.
skill.summary: Run BrowserAct Google Images searches and collect result metadata.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill legitimately uses the BrowserAct API, so the network calls and single environment variable access are expected but still expose search terms and an API credential to a third party. Most SKILL.md external command findings are Markdown formatting false positives, with the actual Python invocation kept as a real command-execution risk. I also found credential-solicitation language that may cause users to paste API keys into chat.

remediation.suggestion: Tell users to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY through a secure environment or secret manager. Do not ask them to paste the key into chat.

remediation.issue: External BrowserAct API calls with bearer token
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact endpoint and data sent. Keep the host fixed to api.browseract.com and never log the Authorization header.

remediation.issue: Local script execution from skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Keep invocation shell-free with a fixed script path and validated numeric arguments. Reject unsupported country and language values before running.

remediation.issue: Result retrieval logic is unreachable after polling
remediation.suggestion: Move timeout handling into the timeout branch so successful tasks reach the result retrieval request.

content.value_statement: Manual image research is slow and hard to repeat across markets. This skill runs BrowserAct image searches and returns structured metadata for review.
actual_capabilities: Reads BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment before starting a task.
Starts a BrowserAct workflow for Google Images with keyword, country, and language inputs.
Configures scroll count and result limit parameters for the workflow.
Polls BrowserAct task status and prints timestamped progress messages.
Defines result fields for titles, sources, thumbnails, links, and result indexes.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct API key in BROWSERACT_API_KEY.
Sends search terms and task metadata to the BrowserAct service.
The script currently exits before retrieving results after a finished status.
Only supports the countries and languages listed in the skill guide.

use_cases.title: Visual Market Research
use_cases.description: Compare image result patterns for product terms across supported regions.

use_cases.title: Competitor Asset Review
use_cases.description: Collect image result titles, sources, and links for competitor brands.

use_cases.title: Creative Reference Gathering
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable list of image references for campaign or design research.

prompt_templates.title: Search One Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Google Images metadata for "modern desk lamps" in the United States. Use English and limit results to 25.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Markets
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Google Images for "running shoes" in the United States and Japan. Summarize source patterns and product signals.

prompt_templates.title: Build Competitor Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect image metadata for three competitor product names. Use supported countries, keep each result set separate, and flag repeated sources.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor Localized Trends
prompt_templates.prompt: Run repeatable searches for five seasonal keywords across France, Germany, and Spain. Return differences in titles, sources, and thumbnail patterns.

output_examples.input: Search for electric bike images in Germany with German language settings.
output_examples.output: A list of German-biased image results with titles, source names, thumbnail links, click-through links, and result positions.

output_examples.input: Compare laptop stand images in the United States and Japan.
output_examples.output: A comparison of visible brands, source domains, product-style listings, and repeated design themes for each locale.

output_examples.input: Track logo image results for a competitor name.
output_examples.output: A review-ready summary of sources, result titles, thumbnails, and links that appear for the competitor query.

best_practices: Use precise keywords and record the country and language used for each run.
Store BrowserAct credentials in environment variables or a secret manager.
Review source links before reusing images in reports or creative work.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys directly into chat or shared logs.
Do not assume thumbnails are licensed for reuse.
Do not run broad unattended searches without a clear result limit.

faq.question: Does this require a BrowserAct account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need a BrowserAct API key available as BROWSERACT_API_KEY.

faq.question: Can it download full-size images?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on metadata, thumbnails, source names, and links from result listings.

faq.question: Can it search by country and language?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports the country and language values listed in the skill instructions.

faq.question: Will it avoid CAPTCHA handling?
faq.answer: The workflow uses BrowserAct automation, so the user does not manage browser CAPTCHA flows directly.

faq.question: Does it send my searches to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. Search terms and workflow parameters are sent to BrowserAct to run the task.

faq.question: Is the current script ready for reliable result retrieval?
faq.answer: Not fully. The polling logic exits before the result retrieval block, so the author should fix it.
